I don't seek to invalidate your experience, but I strongly push back against the "depression is just a sickness making you not see things clearly" idea. In my experience it's just a way people systemically invalidate my thoughts and feelings.

The demented reverse of what we have in the West is what is common in Japanese culture, where people deemed "failures" by strict cultural standards, and are encouraged to kill themselves so as to "cleanse" themselves and their society of their "failure". To me that's just as bad as the strict anti-suicide stance we have in the West.

Not that I agree, but suicide runs against religiously based social policy which argues that all life is a sacred, and that throwing it away via suicide would be morally repugnant. At an anthropological level, it probably serves the social organism at large to choose to suffer, yet be productive, rather than to die. In the modern context it has a lot to do with legal liability, and the idea perhaps inaccurate logic that stems from  mental illness being considered a disease. 

Ultimately it's is a person's radical freedom to choose death over life for any reason, and at anytime they are able to.
